paper_metadata.title: Ductile-brittle transition of carbon alloyed Fe40Mn40Co10Cr10 high entropy alloys

evidence.quote: The mechanical behavior of (Fe 40Mn40Co10Cr10)100-xCx (x = 0, 2.2, 3.3 at.%) high entropy alloys (HEA) at various temperatures (298K, 159K and 77K) was investigated.

while exhibits brittle cleavage fracture characteristic at 77 K (Fig.2d, h), which is consistent with the stress-strain curves.
For C0 HEA, elongation increases with decreasing temperature, with maximum values of 69.5% attained at 77 K.
The elongation of C2.2 HEA increases with decreasing temperature from 298K to 159K, and then decreases after temperature lower than 159K, i.e. maximum elongation (69.1%) is obtained at 159K.
Although the C3.3 HEA has the maximum elongation value (77.8%) among the HEAs at 298K, it shows quite low elongation value of 10.2% at 77 K.

That is to say, the good elongations in these alloys are mainly attributed to twinning induced plasticity (TWIP) [9].
Thus, the better elongation in C0 HEA at 77K arises from both TWIP and TRIP effect.
